pluss::note::make¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::make(text_source values)
Note pluss::note::make(string_range flat, integer_range sizes)
Note pluss::note::make(bool value)
Note pluss::note::make(signed_integer value)
Note pluss::note::make(floating_point value)
Note pluss::note::make(native_values)
Note pluss::note::make(native_values, integer_range sizes)
Note pluss::make_note(text_source values)

The General Typed Entrance To Note¶

make() constructs a homogeneous Note from text, Bool, signed integer, or floating-point input. The source category selects Text, Bool, Int64, or Float64; numeric input is converted once into the Note’s canonical native lane width and is never encoded as text. This makes construction the beginning of a closed Note pipeline rather than an escape into unrelated containers.

For native values, a scalar produces rank zero, a vector or braced list produces rank one, and (flat, sizes) supplies rank-two or rank-three geometry. All signed integer widths converge to Int64 and all floating widths converge to Float64. Bool is stored as contiguous canonical 0/1 lanes rather than std::vector<bool> proxies. Unsigned integers are deliberately not accepted: silently narrowing their full range into Int64 would violate the accuracy-first contract.

text_source is a single converted parameter that accepts every reasonable call-site spelling of “some text”:

  • a bare string literal, std::string_view, std::string, or a single char — one scalar cell, rank 0

  • a braced list of strings — a rank-1 column

  • a nested braced list, two or three levels deep — a rank-2 or rank-3 block

  • a contiguous range of std::string or std::string_view — a rank-1 column

The shape is implied by the call form: nesting depth becomes rank, and the lengths at each level become the sizes. Text is stored as-is, cell by cell; make() does not trim, normalize, case-fold, or re-encode. Multi-byte UTF-8 (accents, CJK, emoji) is preserved intact.

The text overloads always produce NoteDType::Text (encoding=utf8). They label the content as text but do not validate that every byte is well-formed UTF-8. If the source bytes are not valid text, use bytes instead. Bool, signed-integer, and floating-point overloads produce their native dtypes as described above; they do not pass through this text path.

The (flat, sizes) overload¶

When text arrives already flattened from another system — a std::vector of cells plus a separate shape — pass the two ranges directly:

pluss::note::make(flat_range, sizes_range)

Two call-site arguments cannot fold into the single converted text_source parameter, so this is a distinct overload. The flat count must equal the product of sizes; a mismatch is rejected before a Note is built.

pluss::make_note¶

pluss::make_note is the one flat (non-namespaced) spelling kept as a permanent shortcut for the common construct-from-data case, mirroring pluss::make_series and pluss::make_timeline. It takes the same argument forms as pluss::note::make and produces the same result. Every other flat spelling has been retired in favor of pluss::note::*.

Rank ceiling¶

Note is at most 3-dimensional. A four-level nested list, or a sizes range longer than three, is rejected.

The same ceiling and cardinality check applies to native lanes. For example, four values cannot be paired with shape [3, 2]; construction rejects before publishing a partially formed Note.

Native Example: Scalars Keep Their Meaning¶

const auto ready = pluss::note::make(true);
const auto count = pluss::note::make(std::int32_t{42});
const auto score = pluss::note::make(0.875F);

std::cout << std::boolalpha << ready.bool_item() << ' '
          << count.int_item() << ' ' << score.float_item() << '\n';

Output¶

true 42 0.875

Native Example: Flat Values Plus Shape¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<double>{0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});

std::cout << grid << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, dtype=Float64)
[
  [0.5, 1.5],
  [2.5, 3.5]
]

Example 1: A Scalar From A String Literal¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make("Final Exam Review")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Final Exam Review"

The shape is [] (rank 0), not [1]. A scalar Note holds exactly one cell and broadcasts against any shape in later operations.

Example 2: A One-Dimensional Batch¶

const pluss::Note names = pluss::note::make({"Ada Lovelace", "Grace Hopper", "Linus"});
std::cout << names << "\n";  // operator<< uses print()'s default format

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Ada Lovelace", "Grace Hopper", "Linus"]

A braced list of strings is a rank-1 column — the shape most text pipelines start from.

Example 3: A Two-Dimensional Block¶

const pluss::Note grid = pluss::note::make({{"r0c0", "r0c1"}, {"r1c0", "r1c1"}});
pluss::note::print(std::cout, grid) << "\n";  // print(os, n) returns the stream

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["r0c0", "r0c1"], 
  ["r1c0", "r1c1"]
]

Nesting one level deeper adds one axis. Every inner list must be the same length — see Example 10.

Example 4: A Three-Dimensional Block¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({{{"a", "b"}, {"c", "d"}}, {{"e", "f"}, {"g", "h"}}})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2, 2], dim=3, numel=8, encoding=utf8)
[
  [
    ["a", "b"], 
    ["c", "d"]
  ], 
  [
    ["e", "f"], 
    ["g", "h"]
  ]
]

Three levels is the deepest a Note goes.

Example 5: The pluss::make_note Shortcut¶

const pluss::Note stages = pluss::make_note({"draft", "review", "final"});
std::cout << stages << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["draft", "review", "final"]

Identical to pluss::note::make({...}); the flat spelling just reads more naturally at some call sites.

Example 6: A Single char¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note('Q')) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Q"

A lone char is a one-character scalar cell.

Example 7: Flat Storage Plus An Explicit Shape¶

std::vector<std::string> flat{"p", "q", "r", "s", "t", "u"};
std::array<std::int64_t, 2> sizes{2, 3};
const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::make(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::string>(flat),
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes));
pluss::note::print(std::cout, n) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["p", "q", "r"], 
  ["s", "t", "u"]
]

The flat cells fill the shape in row-major order. This is the form to use when the text and its shape come from different sources.

Example 8: Multi-Byte UTF-8 Is Preserved¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::make({"café", "naïve", "日本語", "🎯"});
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["café", "naïve", "日本語", "🎯"]

Every cell keeps its exact bytes. Character-aware length, slicing, and case-mapping are then available as Note methods.

Example 9: The Empty String Is A Valid Scalar¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::make("")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
""

"" is one cell that happens to be empty — distinct from a zero-length Note. empty fills a whole shape with this value.

Example 10: A Ragged Nested List Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::make({{"a", "b"}, {"c"}});
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::make: ragged nested initializer_list is not supported

Every sibling list at a given depth must have the same length; make() does not pad short rows.

Example 11: A Flat/Shape Count Mismatch Is Rejected¶

std::vector<std::string> flat{"a", "b", "c"};
std::array<std::int64_t, 1> sizes{5};
try {
  pluss::note::make(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::string>(flat),
                    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes));
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

Note construction: flat text count must equal the product of the requested sizes

Validation happens before any Note is allocated.

Example 12: A Four-Dimensional List Is Rejected¶

try {
  pluss::note::make({{{{"a"}}}});
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

pluss::note::make: supports up to 3D nested initializer_list

  • pluss::note::from_lines / pluss::note::from_words: build a 1-D Note by splitting a single string.

  • pluss::note::print: render a Note for inspection.
